digest.component_or_area: codebase refactoring and consolidation across store paths, commands, engine, and utilities
propositions: Duplicated decision logic exists in 2–7 places throughout the codebase; fixes landed in one copy leave twin implementations broken, causing families of identical bugs to arrive as multi-ticket instalments

Consolidation children must collapse each duplicated computation into one shared module, preserve all pinned observable behavior verified by named pinning tests, and include a construct-uniqueness guard test that asserts the construct appears only once (modulo explicit escape markers)

Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC3 are stated as proxy metrics ('tests only additions' and 'net non-test lines negative') that legitimate consolidation work violates; the actual guarantees are 'no pinned behavior changes' and 'exactly one implementation per construct', already enforced by per-child construct-uniqueness tests

Eight of thirteen consolidation children have merged with net +241 non-test lines and expected test-file deletions where duplicated test helpers were consolidated, both contradicting AC2/AC3 as written but confirming the consolidation strategy is correct
